header:
Rutgers University-New Brunswick
United States · Mathematics PhD
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• This dossier is for New Brunswick, not the separate Newark or Camden admissions programs.
• Prepare a CV despite the FAQ’s optional wording.
• GRE mathematics is optional but explicitly encouraged; omission is not described consistently.
• Funding sources contain materially different dates and rates.
• An English admission waiver does not establish TA spoken-English certification.
• Faculty entries identify research fit, not a commitment to supervise.
• Chi Li’s current Johns Hopkins author page lists Research Professor and Fall 2026 teaching there; exclude him
from the ordinary Rutgers adviser list despite stale Rutgers references.
• Stephen D. Miller is currently labeled Research Visitor in Rutgers’ directory; his personal page directs
post-July 2025 correspondence to Yeshiva. Confirm any Rutgers supervisory role separately.
• Henryk Iwaniec, Jozsef Beck and Charles Weibel are emeritus; they are not presented as ordinary
new-adviser options.
• James Lepowsky and Konstantin Matveev have current faculty appointments, but the latest papers verified in
inspected institutional records were from 2017 and 2021 respectively. More recent work remains an explicit
gap.

sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
An international applicant may apply to the full-time, fall-entry PhD with a completed bachelor’s degree and
preparation comparable to an honors mathematics major. A mathematics degree is not formally required. A
UChicago mathematics bachelor’s is eligible in principle if completed by enrollment; admission remains
competitive and F1 status is not itself an exclusion. [s1] [s2] [s3]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Select Mathematics, PhD, New Brunswick, Fall 2027 in the central application; create a CommunityID; prepare
transcripts, statement, CV and referee details. Ask referees before completing their section, which triggers
invitations. Select financial-aid consideration if wanted. Arrange English-waiver evidence and resolve any
checklist requirement with graduate admissions. Apply through the central portal rather than sending an
application to the department. [s1] [s2] [s4] [s5] [s6]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
Contact with a genuinely relevant faculty member can help clarify fit, but prior supervisor consent is not a
listed prerequisite for the ordinary mathematics PhD. Check current appointment and capacity before writing.
Lisa Marquand’s current research page explicitly welcomes email conversations about her work. [s1] [s2] [s17]
[s19]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Use the central graduate application and status pages. Check core information before submission because
corrections can require admissions intervention. Upload initial records under Education History; arrange

institution-sent official records when required. Track receipts and use referee reminders through the portal. [s5]
[s6] [s7] [s8]
Cycle verification [2027 confirmed]
The central mathematics program listing explicitly publishes Fall 2027 and Fall 2028 deadlines; the
departmental FAQ explicitly mentions January 1, 2027 for GRE uploads. Much other guidance is standing policy,
and financial pages mix 2013, 2025-26 and Fall 2026 information. Do not silently promote those amounts or
rules to a guaranteed Fall 2027 offer. [s1] [s3] [s9] [s10] [s12]

sections.title: Deadlines by stage
sections.text:
Academic application [2027 confirmed]
December 15, 2026 for Fall 2027, for both US and non-US applicants. The program also publishes December
15, 2027 for Fall 2028. A cutoff time and time zone are not stated. The department may accept late
applications, but full consideration is not assured; do not plan around late acceptance. [s1] [s2]
Funding consideration [Standing rule]
Use December 15, 2026 for full consideration for admission and ordinary departmental financial support. No
distinct ordinary funding application deadline is published in the reviewed pages. Internal or named fellowship
nomination deadlines must be checked separately. [s1] [s2] [s10]
Reference receipt [Standing rule]
Target December 15 with the application. The departmental FAQ permits late references no later than January
1, sent as a PDF through the admissions contact form with applicant name and RUID. That paragraph does not
state the year or time zone; confirm that January 1, 2027 is the applicable grace cutoff rather than relying on it.
[s1] [s3]
Test-score receipt [Conflict]
The FAQ explicitly allows GRE scores to be uploaded before January 1, 2027. It permits unofficial scores for
departmental review and official scores after admission/acceptance. Central instructions, especially for English
proficiency, call for official reporting and warn that unofficial scores may not be reviewable. Resolve any
unwaived English requirement before the application deadline. Rutgers ETS institution code is 2790; no
department code is required. [s3] [s4] [s5] [s6]
Supporting documents [Standing rule]
December 15, 2026 is the application-review target. The portal permits later supporting-material uploads, but
a universal final cutoff for non-reference materials is not published. Final official transcripts and evidence of the
awarded degree are required after acceptance; the offer/checklist supplies the exact enrollment deadline. [s1]
[s2] [s7] [s8]
Accepting an offer [Unresolved]
No explicit Fall 2027 acceptance or funding-commitment date was located in the reviewed mathematics pages
or handbook. Follow the written admission/funding offer and verify any interim response requirement; do not
infer a universal April 15 deadline from older affiliations. [s7] [s9] [s10] [s12]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Standing rule]
Central minimum TOEFL section scores for tests through January 21, 2026: writing 22, speaking 23, reading 21,
listening 17. For tests from January 22, 2026: writing 4.5, speaking 4.5, reading 4, listening 4. IELTS minimum
is 7; the page gives a Duolingo range of 120-130, so confirm the applicable program threshold if using it.
Scores must fall within two years of the semester start. Teaching assistants face a separate spoken-English
assessment/training process; an admission waiver does not establish teaching certification. [s4] [s14]

UChicago English exemption [Conflict]
A completed UChicago degree taught entirely in English supports a central, case-by-case waiver request.
Central instructions require an official transcript or registrar’s English-instruction letter sent directly. The
mathematics FAQ describes an undergraduate-English-study exception of three years, creating uncertainty for
an applicant whose bachelor’s is still in progress. Obtain written approval and confirm that the portal removes
the requirement; use https://go.rutgers.edu/emailgrad for admissions contact. [s3] [s4]
GRE General [Standing rule]
Optional; neither the central program listing nor department requires the GRE General Test. [s1] [s2] [s3]
GRE Mathematics [Conflict]
Not required, but the department highly recommends the mathematics subject test and describes it as
carrying substantial weight. The FAQ also says absence of GRE scores will not hurt an application. These
statements are not equivalent to an indifferent or prohibited policy; confirm how the Fall 2027 committee
reconciles them. [s1] [s2] [s3]

Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
Submit transcripts for all postsecondary institutions. Unofficial copies are used for initial review; after
acceptance, arrange institution-sent official final records showing the degree award. Electronic vendors include
Parchment, eScrip-Safe and National Student Clearinghouse; the central address is
e-transcripts@gradadm.rutgers.edu. Study-abroad records may be covered by the home transcript if it lists
courses, grades and transfer credit; otherwise supply the separate record. [s5] [s7] [s8]

Not listed as a separate required item in the public mathematics program checklist. This does not establish
that an optional upload is accepted, nor does it resolve additional questions visible only inside the live

sections.title: Recommendation letters
sections.text:
Number and type [Standing rule]
At least three letters; additional letters may be submitted. Choose referees who can evaluate mathematical
preparation and potential for doctoral research. [s1] [s2] [s3]
Scholarship references [Unresolved]
No extra reference is publicly specified for ordinary departmental support. Additional referees or distinct
questions for named scholarships cannot be established without the current nomination/application form. [s1]
[s10] [s15]
What sends the invitation [Standing rule]
Completing the Recommendations section sends the electronic requests to the referees. Obtain their consent
before completing that section. [s6]
Before versus after submission [Standing rule]
Invitations are not restricted to after final submission: the completed Recommendations section triggers them.
Paper or later replacement procedures require the applicant’s identifying details/RUID. [s6] [s7]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
The applicant-status portal reports received references, transcripts and scores. It provides a Resend Form
function for reminders. Allow central processing time, stated as approximately two weeks for official materials,
before requesting a missing-item investigation. [s7]
Updating and reusing letters [Standing rule]
Central status instructions describe adding/changing a recommender through the recommendation form. The

mathematics FAQ allows reuse of letters from a prior master’s application while encouraging letters directed to
doctoral study. Whether a submitted electronic letter can be overwritten, or automatically reused across
different cycles, is not publicly resolved. [s3] [s7]

sections.title: Written materials
sections.text:
Academic CV / resume [Conflict]
Prepare and upload a CV/resume: the central program checklist requires it, while the mathematics FAQ calls it
optional. The conflicting labels make omission risky. No public length or formatting limit was found. The FAQ
permits a later updated resume in an OTHER upload, clearly labeled as an updated resume. [s1] [s3] [s8]
Statement of purpose [Standing rule]
A personal statement serving as the statement of purpose is required. Prompt, paraphrased: explain reasons
for pursuing doctoral mathematics and choosing Rutgers, mathematical interests, previous research and
possible research directions; an explanation of weak grades may be included if useful. Be specific and concise.
The public pages give no numerical length, font or spacing limit. Use the live portal to capture the exact final
prompt before drafting; a later replacement statement can be uploaded. [s1] [s3] [s5]
Personal / background statement [Standing rule]
The required personal statement is the academic purpose statement above. A distinct background,
personal-history or diversity essay is not separately listed in the public mathematics requirements; portal-only
questions remain unverified. [s1] [s5]
Research-interest statement [Standing rule]
Discuss mathematical interests and possible research directions within the required statement. No separate
research-interest essay or numerical limit is publicly specified. [s1] [s5]
Research proposal; Publications list; Course-list document [Standing rule]
Not listed as a separate required item in the public mathematics program checklist. This does not establish
that an optional upload is accepted, nor does it resolve additional questions visible only inside the live
application. [s1] [s2]
Writing sample / thesis / research summary [Standing rule]
A writing sample or research paper is optional according to the departmental FAQ. Central uploads permit
multiple items with different filenames. No public sample length, format or topic rule was located; do not
substitute a web link for an upload without checking the live form. [s3] [s8]
Scholarship essays [Unresolved]
No separate essay is publicly required for ordinary mathematics assistantship/fellowship consideration. Exact
2027 prompts, limits and additional questions for named awards were not found in public forms and require
confirmation. [s1] [s10] [s15]
Other short answers / materials [Standing rule]
Check all short answers in the live mathematics application. If an unrequested item has no suitable upload slot,
ask admissions how to supply it. The publicly linked October 2025 sample is for the Master of Business and
Science and does not establish the mathematics application’s prompts or limits. [s5] [s8] [s20]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Conflict]
The mathematics prospective-student page reports a Fall 2026 TA stipend of USD 40,000 for ten months, with
staff health benefits; it describes fellowship stipends of USD 30,000-35,000 with different insurance. These are
not verified Fall 2027 offers. An older mathematics page still quotes USD 25,969 for nine months from 2013
and must not be used as a current rate. The October 2025 SGS handbook gives an internal fellowship floor of
USD 30,833 per academic year or USD 37,000 per calendar year, requiring reconciliation with the department’s
lower fellowship figure. Tuition is normally covered; exact fees, insurance contributions, taxes and summer
funding depend on the offer. [s9] [s10] [s12] [s13]
Years of support [Conflict]
The SAS appointment memo provides five years of university support, subject to satisfactory progress, for PhD
entrants from Fall 2024 who receive university funding in year one. Its guarantee does not extend on the same
basis to externally funded first-year students. Older mathematics text describes an initial two-year
commitment, annual renewal, priority through year five and a six-year university support cap. Obtain a written
Fall 2027 guarantee that resolves this mismatch. [s10] [s11] [s12]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
International applicants may be considered for ordinary departmental TA, GA and fellowship funding. Eligibility
for each named award may impose additional conditions; a reference to fellowships for US applicants on one
page is not evidence that all departmental funding excludes international students. [s2] [s10]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Renewal depends on academic progress and satisfactory assigned duties. Teaching appointments require the
relevant English assessment and training. Older mathematics support text ties progress to written qualifying
examinations by year two and the oral examination by year three; verify the current handbook and individual
offer for binding milestones. [s10] [s11] [s14]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
Request financial aid within the main application for ordinary departmental consideration; no separate ordinary
funding essay/application is publicly specified. Applicants relying on external support or seeking a change in
support should communicate with the graduate director. Named awards may require internal nomination. [s1]
[s2] [s10] [s15]
Other funding routes [Prior cycle]
Potential supplements include summer teaching when available, advanced-student faculty grants, research
internships/REU work and GradFund assistance with external awards. The 2025-26 Presidential Fellowship page
describes a USD 10,000 annual supplement for up to three years, rather than an independent tuition/health
package; summer use is possible. The 2027 rate, nomination schedule and international eligibility require
confirmation. [s13] [s15] [s16]
Application fee [Standing rule]
USD 70, nonrefundable. Payment follows submission by credit card or e-check; selecting pay later does not
make an unpaid application ready for review. [s5] [s6]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
Central waiver categories include McNair, Project 1000, qualifying GEM/scholarship programs and military
eligibility, selected in the Financial Information section with required evidence. The mathematics graduate
director may seek SGS hardship assistance, but approval is not guaranteed. F1 status alone is not a published
waiver basis. [s3] [s5] [s6]

sections.title: Potential advisers and recent research
sections.text:
1. Algebraic geometry and complex algebraic geometry
Lev Borisov
Toric geometry, derived categories and explicit algebraic surfaces, including fake projective planes. [s17] [s19]
[s21]
Distinguished Professor; prospective-student capacity not published.
Research evidence: 2025 preprint · Finding equations of the fake projective plane (C18,p=3,{2I})
Selected recent verified paper; a preprint is not represented as a refereed publication.
Anders Skovsted Buch
Schubert calculus, homogeneous spaces, quantum K-theory and Gromov-Witten invariants. [s17] [s19] [s22]
Current Rutgers New Brunswick faculty; Fall 2027 supervision availability is not publicly established.
Research evidence: 2025, Pacific Journal of Mathematics 338, 209-229 · Equivariant rigidity of Richardson varieties
Selected recent verified paper; a preprint is not represented as a refereed publication.
Lisa Nicole Marquand
Cubic fourfolds, hyperkähler varieties, Hodge theory, birational geometry and derived equivalences. [s17] [s19]
[s23] [s43]
Assistant Professor, joined Rutgers in Fall 2026. Her author research page welcomes email discussion; verify Fall 2027 capacity.
Research evidence: 2026 preprint, revised October 19 · Birational cubic fourfolds via an Enriques Cremona transformation
Selected recent verified paper; a preprint is not represented as a refereed publication.
Christopher Woodward
Symplectic and algebraic geometry, Lie theory, moduli spaces, quantum K-theory, tropical geometry and
Fukaya categories. [s17] [s19] [s24]
Distinguished Professor. Current home page lists Fall 2026/Spring 2027 appointment-based office hours; papers page is explicitly
archival as of April 20, 2026.
Research evidence: April 2026 author version · Holomorphic disks and tropical Lagrangians
Selected recent verified paper; a preprint is not represented as a refereed publication.

Guangbo Xu
Symplectic geometry, gauge theory, Gromov-Witten/Floer theory and algebraic-geometric connections through
blowups and gauged models. [s17] [s19] [s25]
Associate Professor; symplectic geometry is an adjacent rather than primarily arithmetic fit.
Research evidence: 2025, Journal of the Institute of Mathematics of Jussieu · Fukaya categories of blowups
Selected recent verified paper; a preprint is not represented as a refereed publication.
2. Number theory and arithmetic geometry
Matthew P. Young
Analytic number theory, automorphic L-functions, moment estimates, subconvexity and spectral trace
formulas. [s17] [s19] [s26]
Harold H. Martin Professor at Rutgers; do not rely on an older Texas A&M affiliation.
Research evidence: 2026, Forum of Mathematics, Sigma · A generalized PGL(2) Petersson/Bruggeman/Kuznetsov formula for
analytic applications
Selected recent verified paper; a preprint is not represented as a refereed publication.
Alex Kontorovich
Analytic number theory, automorphic representations, arithmetic and thin groups, hyperbolic geometry and
spectral/homogeneous dynamics. [s17] [s19] [s27] [s42]
Distinguished Professor and department chair for 2026-29; confirm supervisory capacity during the chair term.
Research evidence: 2026, submitted · Arithmetic Polyhedra
Selected recent verified paper; a preprint is not represented as a refereed publication.
3. Representation theory and algebra
Lisa Carbone
Infinite-dimensional Kac-Moody groups and Lie theory, arithmetic quotients, Eisenstein series and connections
with mathematical physics. [s17] [s19] [s28]
Current Rutgers New Brunswick faculty; Fall 2027 supervision availability is not publicly established.
Research evidence: 2026, Forum Mathematicum 38(4), 1257-1296 · Eisenstein series on arithmetic quotients of rank 2
Kac-Moody groups over finite fields
Selected recent verified paper; a preprint is not represented as a refereed publication.
Yi-Zhi Huang
Vertex operator algebras, tensor categories, twisted modules, orbifold conformal field theory and geometric
applications. [s17] [s19] [s29]
Current Rutgers New Brunswick faculty; Fall 2027 supervision availability is not publicly established.
Research evidence: 2026, SIGMA 22, 086 · Twisted intertwining operators and tensor products of (generalized) twisted
modules
Selected recent verified paper; a preprint is not represented as a refereed publication.
James Lepowsky
Vertex operator algebras, infinite-dimensional Lie theory and representation-theoretic/combinatorial identities.
[s17] [s19] [s30] [s41]
Distinguished Professor; Spring 2026 vertex-algebra teaching confirms current activity. The newest paper verified in the
inspected institutional record is historical (2017), so recent publication activity and new-student capacity remain unresolved.
Research evidence: 2017, Ramanujan Journal 42(1), 97-129 · A motivated proof of the Göllnitz-Gordon-Andrews identities
Selected recent verified paper; a preprint is not represented as a refereed publication.

Vladimir Retakh
Noncommutative algebra, cluster structures, marked surfaces and homological/algebraic methods. [s17] [s19]
[s31]
Current Rutgers New Brunswick faculty; Fall 2027 supervision availability is not publicly established.
Research evidence: 2025 preprint · Noncommutative marked surfaces II: tagged triangulations, clusters, and their symmetries
Selected recent verified paper; a preprint is not represented as a refereed publication.
Siddhartha Sahi
Representation theory and harmonic analysis, root systems, special functions and
Macdonald/Opdam-Cherednik theory. [s17] [s19] [s32]
Distinguished Professor; current Rutgers seminar documents the paper and September 17, 2026 presentation.
Research evidence: 2026 preprint · The Opdam-Cherednik kernel is the Laplace transform of a positive measure
Selected recent verified paper; a preprint is not represented as a refereed publication.
Pham Huu Tiep
Representations and character theory of finite groups of Lie type, with arithmetic-geometric work on
exponential sums and monodromy groups. [s17] [s19] [s33]
Joshua Barlaz Distinguished Professor; strong bridge between finite-group representation theory and arithmetic monodromy.
Research evidence: 2025, Forum of Mathematics, Sigma 13, e101 · Moments, exponential sums, and monodromy groups
Selected recent verified paper; a preprint is not represented as a refereed publication.
Damiano Rossi
Modular representation theory, finite groups of Lie type and local-to-global conjectures. [s17] [s19] [s34]
Assistant Professor; current Fall 2026 Deligne-Lusztig teaching corroborates the research fit.
Research evidence: 2026, Algebra & Number Theory 20(2), 333-382 · The Alperin Weight Conjecture and the Glauberman
correspondence via character triples
Selected recent verified paper; a preprint is not represented as a refereed publication.
Konstantin Matveev
Symmetric functions, asymptotic representation theory, integrable probability and interacting particle systems.
[s17] [s19] [s35]
Assistant Professor; an adjacent representation/probability fit. The most recent paper verified in the inspected institutional record
is from 2021, so newer publication activity remains unverified.
Research evidence: 2021, International Mathematics Research Notices 2021(3), 2210-2249 · The q-Hahn PushTASEP
Selected recent verified paper; a preprint is not represented as a refereed publication.
Haisheng Li
Vertex and quantum vertex algebras, affine Lie algebras and their module theories. [s17] [s19] [s36]
Professor at Rutgers Camden; the New Brunswick research-area page explicitly lists him as a graduate-faculty affiliate. Confirm
cross-campus supervision arrangements and availability before treating him as a New Brunswick adviser.
Research evidence: 2026, Communications in Mathematical Physics 407(5), article 103 · Twisted Quantum Affine Algebras and
Equivariant ϕ-Coordinated Modules for Quantum Vertex Algebras
Selected recent verified paper; a preprint is not represented as a refereed publication.
4. Complex geometry and geometric analysis
Jian Song
Kähler geometry, Kähler-Ricci flow, singular metrics, complex Monge-Ampère equations and analytic geometry
of minimal models. [s17] [s19] [s37]

Distinguished Professor; current author publication page links the October 2026 preprint.
Research evidence: 2026 preprint · Type I estimates for the Kähler-Ricci flow II
Selected recent verified paper; a preprint is not represented as a refereed publication.
Xiaojun Huang
Several complex variables, CR geometry, holomorphic mapping rigidity and Bergman/Kähler geometry. [s17]
[s19] [s38] [s44]
Distinguished Professor. Official May 2026 seminar descriptions also corroborate active work on Bergman metrics and Stein
manifolds.
Research evidence: 2026, Acta Mathematica Sinica, English Series 42(5), 1283-1298 · Regular Types and Order of Vanishing
along a Set of Non-integrable Vector Fields
Selected recent verified paper; a preprint is not represented as a refereed publication.

Pay attention to
• This dossier is for New Brunswick, not the separate Newark or Camden admissions programs.
• Prepare a CV despite the FAQ’s optional wording.
• GRE mathematics is optional but explicitly encouraged; omission is not described consistently.
• Funding sources contain materially different dates and rates.
• An English admission waiver does not establish TA spoken-English certification.
• Faculty entries identify research fit, not a commitment to supervise.
• Chi Li’s current Johns Hopkins author page lists Research Professor and Fall 2026 teaching there; exclude him
from the ordinary Rutgers adviser list despite stale Rutgers references.
• Stephen D. Miller is currently labeled Research Visitor in Rutgers’ directory; his personal page directs
post-July 2025 correspondence to Yeshiva. Confirm any Rutgers supervisory role separately.
• Henryk Iwaniec, Jozsef Beck and Charles Weibel are emeritus; they are not presented as ordinary
new-adviser options.
• James Lepowsky and Konstantin Matveev have current faculty appointments, but the latest papers verified in
inspected institutional records were from 2017 and 2021 respectively. More recent work remains an explicit
gap.
Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
An international applicant may apply to the full-time, fall-entry PhD with a completed bachelor’s degree and
preparation comparable to an honors mathematics major. A mathematics degree is not formally required. A
UChicago mathematics bachelor’s is eligible in principle if completed by enrollment; admission remains
competitive and F1 status is not itself an exclusion. [s1] [s2] [s3]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Select Mathematics, PhD, New Brunswick, Fall 2027 in the central application; create a CommunityID; prepare
transcripts, statement, CV and referee details. Ask referees before completing their section, which triggers
invitations. Select financial-aid consideration if wanted. Arrange English-waiver evidence and resolve any
checklist requirement with graduate admissions. Apply through the central portal rather than sending an
application to the department. [s1] [s2] [s4] [s5] [s6]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
Contact with a genuinely relevant faculty member can help clarify fit, but prior supervisor consent is not a
listed prerequisite for the ordinary mathematics PhD. Check current appointment and capacity before writing.
Lisa Marquand’s current research page explicitly welcomes email conversations about her work. [s1] [s2] [s17]
[s19]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Use the central graduate application and status pages. Check core information before submission because
corrections can require admissions intervention. Upload initial records under Education History; arrange

institution-sent official records when required. Track receipts and use referee reminders through the portal. [s5]
[s6] [s7] [s8]
Cycle verification [2027 confirmed]
The central mathematics program listing explicitly publishes Fall 2027 and Fall 2028 deadlines; the
departmental FAQ explicitly mentions January 1, 2027 for GRE uploads. Much other guidance is standing policy,
and financial pages mix 2013, 2025-26 and Fall 2026 information. Do not silently promote those amounts or
rules to a guaranteed Fall 2027 offer. [s1] [s3] [s9] [s10] [s12]
Deadlines by stage
Academic application [2027 confirmed]
December 15, 2026 for Fall 2027, for both US and non-US applicants. The program also publishes December
15, 2027 for Fall 2028. A cutoff time and time zone are not stated. The department may accept late
applications, but full consideration is not assured; do not plan around late acceptance. [s1] [s2]
Funding consideration [Standing rule]
Use December 15, 2026 for full consideration for admission and ordinary departmental financial support. No
distinct ordinary funding application deadline is published in the reviewed pages. Internal or named fellowship
nomination deadlines must be checked separately. [s1] [s2] [s10]
Reference receipt [Standing rule]
Target December 15 with the application. The departmental FAQ permits late references no later than January
1, sent as a PDF through the admissions contact form with applicant name and RUID. That paragraph does not
state the year or time zone; confirm that January 1, 2027 is the applicable grace cutoff rather than relying on it.
[s1] [s3]
Test-score receipt [Conflict]
The FAQ explicitly allows GRE scores to be uploaded before January 1, 2027. It permits unofficial scores for
departmental review and official scores after admission/acceptance. Central instructions, especially for English
proficiency, call for official reporting and warn that unofficial scores may not be reviewable. Resolve any
unwaived English requirement before the application deadline. Rutgers ETS institution code is 2790; no
department code is required. [s3] [s4] [s5] [s6]
Supporting documents [Standing rule]
December 15, 2026 is the application-review target. The portal permits later supporting-material uploads, but
a universal final cutoff for non-reference materials is not published. Final official transcripts and evidence of the
awarded degree are required after acceptance; the offer/checklist supplies the exact enrollment deadline. [s1]
[s2] [s7] [s8]
Accepting an offer [Unresolved]
No explicit Fall 2027 acceptance or funding-commitment date was located in the reviewed mathematics pages
or handbook. Follow the written admission/funding offer and verify any interim response requirement; do not
infer a universal April 15 deadline from older affiliations. [s7] [s9] [s10] [s12]
English and GRE
English requirement [Standing rule]
Central minimum TOEFL section scores for tests through January 21, 2026: writing 22, speaking 23, reading 21,
listening 17. For tests from January 22, 2026: writing 4.5, speaking 4.5, reading 4, listening 4. IELTS minimum
is 7; the page gives a Duolingo range of 120-130, so confirm the applicable program threshold if using it.
Scores must fall within two years of the semester start. Teaching assistants face a separate spoken-English
assessment/training process; an admission waiver does not establish teaching certification. [s4] [s14]

UChicago English exemption [Conflict]
A completed UChicago degree taught entirely in English supports a central, case-by-case waiver request.
Central instructions require an official transcript or registrar’s English-instruction letter sent directly. The
mathematics FAQ describes an undergraduate-English-study exception of three years, creating uncertainty for
an applicant whose bachelor’s is still in progress. Obtain written approval and confirm that the portal removes
the requirement; use https://go.rutgers.edu/emailgrad for admissions contact. [s3] [s4]
GRE General [Standing rule]
Optional; neither the central program listing nor department requires the GRE General Test. [s1] [s2] [s3]
GRE Mathematics [Conflict]
Not required, but the department highly recommends the mathematics subject test and describes it as
carrying substantial weight. The FAQ also says absence of GRE scores will not hurt an application. These
statements are not equivalent to an indifferent or prohibited policy; confirm how the Fall 2027 committee
reconciles them. [s1] [s2] [s3]
Academic records
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
Submit transcripts for all postsecondary institutions. Unofficial copies are used for initial review; after
acceptance, arrange institution-sent official final records showing the degree award. Electronic vendors include
Parchment, eScrip-Safe and National Student Clearinghouse; the central address is
e-transcripts@gradadm.rutgers.edu. Study-abroad records may be covered by the home transcript if it lists
courses, grades and transfer credit; otherwise supply the separate record. [s5] [s7] [s8]
Mathematics-course list; Course descriptions [Standing rule]
Not listed as a separate required item in the public mathematics program checklist. This does not establish
that an optional upload is accepted, nor does it resolve additional questions visible only inside the live
application. [s1] [s2]
Recommendation letters
Number and type [Standing rule]
At least three letters; additional letters may be submitted. Choose referees who can evaluate mathematical
preparation and potential for doctoral research. [s1] [s2] [s3]
Scholarship references [Unresolved]
No extra reference is publicly specified for ordinary departmental support. Additional referees or distinct
questions for named scholarships cannot be established without the current nomination/application form. [s1]
[s10] [s15]
What sends the invitation [Standing rule]
Completing the Recommendations section sends the electronic requests to the referees. Obtain their consent
before completing that section. [s6]
Before versus after submission [Standing rule]
Invitations are not restricted to after final submission: the completed Recommendations section triggers them.
Paper or later replacement procedures require the applicant’s identifying details/RUID. [s6] [s7]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
The applicant-status portal reports received references, transcripts and scores. It provides a Resend Form
function for reminders. Allow central processing time, stated as approximately two weeks for official materials,
before requesting a missing-item investigation. [s7]
Updating and reusing letters [Standing rule]
Central status instructions describe adding/changing a recommender through the recommendation form. The

mathematics FAQ allows reuse of letters from a prior master’s application while encouraging letters directed to
doctoral study. Whether a submitted electronic letter can be overwritten, or automatically reused across
different cycles, is not publicly resolved. [s3] [s7]
Written materials
Academic CV / resume [Conflict]
Prepare and upload a CV/resume: the central program checklist requires it, while the mathematics FAQ calls it
optional. The conflicting labels make omission risky. No public length or formatting limit was found. The FAQ
permits a later updated resume in an OTHER upload, clearly labeled as an updated resume. [s1] [s3] [s8]
Statement of purpose [Standing rule]
A personal statement serving as the statement of purpose is required. Prompt, paraphrased: explain reasons
for pursuing doctoral mathematics and choosing Rutgers, mathematical interests, previous research and
possible research directions; an explanation of weak grades may be included if useful. Be specific and concise.
The public pages give no numerical length, font or spacing limit. Use the live portal to capture the exact final
prompt before drafting; a later replacement statement can be uploaded. [s1] [s3] [s5]
Personal / background statement [Standing rule]
The required personal statement is the academic purpose statement above. A distinct background,
personal-history or diversity essay is not separately listed in the public mathematics requirements; portal-only
questions remain unverified. [s1] [s5]
Research-interest statement [Standing rule]
Discuss mathematical interests and possible research directions within the required statement. No separate
research-interest essay or numerical limit is publicly specified. [s1] [s5]
Research proposal; Publications list; Course-list document [Standing rule]
Not listed as a separate required item in the public mathematics program checklist. This does not establish
that an optional upload is accepted, nor does it resolve additional questions visible only inside the live
application. [s1] [s2]
Writing sample / thesis / research summary [Standing rule]
A writing sample or research paper is optional according to the departmental FAQ. Central uploads permit
multiple items with different filenames. No public sample length, format or topic rule was located; do not
substitute a web link for an upload without checking the live form. [s3] [s8]
Scholarship essays [Unresolved]
No separate essay is publicly required for ordinary mathematics assistantship/fellowship consideration. Exact
2027 prompts, limits and additional questions for named awards were not found in public forms and require
confirmation. [s1] [s10] [s15]
Other short answers / materials [Standing rule]
Check all short answers in the live mathematics application. If an unrequested item has no suitable upload slot,
ask admissions how to supply it. The publicly linked October 2025 sample is for the Master of Business and
Science and does not establish the mathematics application’s prompts or limits. [s5] [s8] [s20]

Funding and fees
Amount and coverage [Conflict]
The mathematics prospective-student page reports a Fall 2026 TA stipend of USD 40,000 for ten months, with
staff health benefits; it describes fellowship stipends of USD 30,000-35,000 with different insurance. These are
not verified Fall 2027 offers. An older mathematics page still quotes USD 25,969 for nine months from 2013
and must not be used as a current rate. The October 2025 SGS handbook gives an internal fellowship floor of
USD 30,833 per academic year or USD 37,000 per calendar year, requiring reconciliation with the department’s
lower fellowship figure. Tuition is normally covered; exact fees, insurance contributions, taxes and summer
funding depend on the offer. [s9] [s10] [s12] [s13]
Years of support [Conflict]
The SAS appointment memo provides five years of university support, subject to satisfactory progress, for PhD
entrants from Fall 2024 who receive university funding in year one. Its guarantee does not extend on the same
basis to externally funded first-year students. Older mathematics text describes an initial two-year
commitment, annual renewal, priority through year five and a six-year university support cap. Obtain a written
Fall 2027 guarantee that resolves this mismatch. [s10] [s11] [s12]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
International applicants may be considered for ordinary departmental TA, GA and fellowship funding. Eligibility
for each named award may impose additional conditions; a reference to fellowships for US applicants on one
page is not evidence that all departmental funding excludes international students. [s2] [s10]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Renewal depends on academic progress and satisfactory assigned duties. Teaching appointments require the
relevant English assessment and training. Older mathematics support text ties progress to written qualifying
examinations by year two and the oral examination by year three; verify the current handbook and individual
offer for binding milestones. [s10] [s11] [s14]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
Request financial aid within the main application for ordinary departmental consideration; no separate ordinary
funding essay/application is publicly specified. Applicants relying on external support or seeking a change in
support should communicate with the graduate director. Named awards may require internal nomination. [s1]
[s2] [s10] [s15]
Other funding routes [Prior cycle]
Potential supplements include summer teaching when available, advanced-student faculty grants, research
internships/REU work and GradFund assistance with external awards. The 2025-26 Presidential Fellowship page
describes a USD 10,000 annual supplement for up to three years, rather than an independent tuition/health
package; summer use is possible. The 2027 rate, nomination schedule and international eligibility require
confirmation. [s13] [s15] [s16]
Application fee [Standing rule]
USD 70, nonrefundable. Payment follows submission by credit card or e-check; selecting pay later does not
make an unpaid application ready for review. [s5] [s6]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
Central waiver categories include McNair, Project 1000, qualifying GEM/scholarship programs and military
eligibility, selected in the Financial Information section with required evidence. The mathematics graduate
director may seek SGS hardship assistance, but approval is not guaranteed. F1 status alone is not a published
waiver basis. [s3] [s5] [s6]

Conflicts and remaining checks
Conflicting sources [Conflict]
Resolve the CV required/optional mismatch; GRE-math strong recommendation versus no-disadvantage
language; central completed-degree versus departmental English-study waiver wording; unofficial-score review
versus central official-score requirements; and divergent stipend and support-duration statements. Current
faculty appointments also supersede stale research-group listings: Chi Li is at Johns Hopkins, Stephen Miller is
a Rutgers research visitor, and Iwaniec, Beck and Weibel are emeritus. [s1] [s2] [s3] [s4] [s9] [s10] [s11] [s12] [s17]
[s18] [s39] [s40]
Checks still needed [Unresolved]
Confirm the application time zone; applicability of the January 1 reference grace date; English waiver while the
degree is in progress; GRE-math weighting; CV/statement limits and live short answers; final official-record and
commitment dates; the full 2027 funding package; named-award forms; submitted-letter replacement and
cross-cycle reuse; and each potential adviser’s availability. No unverified portal-only rule has been filled with a
generic assumption. [s1] [s2] [s3] [s4] [s7] [s9] [s11] [s15]
